newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance lifts Delhi shares to close higher.
newsitem.headline: Reliance lifts Delhi shares to close higher.

text.p: Strong buying in textile and petrochemical giant Reliance Industries drove Delhi stocks to a higher close on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 13.46 points higher at 893.41 points.
"Frantic purchases by foreign investors in select blue chips like Reliance Industries brought back buoyancy into the market," a broker said.
Reliance Industries closed 12.10 rupees higher at 361.35.
"It seems that the market is heading for another bull run largely in anticipations of political stability," said Ashok Kaul of brokers Rajpaul Chadha and Company.
Traders said prospects of an end to the prevailing political uncertainty also spurred buying.

Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), a regional party in the ruling United Front (UF) coalition threatened last week it would withdraw from the government if a breakaway faction of the UF, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), was not admitted to the coalition.
An Indian newspaper reported on Wednesday that the DMK will not be rigid in its stand in pursuing the RJD issue.
Brokers said the recommendation of an easier carry-forward trading system by a committee set up by stock market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India, also boosted the market.
Hindustan Lever closed 34.45 rupees higher at 1,365.00.
